text:
sam: Quick ask from last night's client dinner in Madrid. Paid on corporate card but the restaurant only gave a handwritten receipt with no VAT breakdown and I forgot to get the itemized check (we shared bottles). Also one colleague paid for a personal dessert separately on their card. Can I submit the handwritten receipt + a split note?
people-ops: Yes, handwritten receipts accepted if legible. For shared meals: submit one claim with separate lines per person or ask the teammate who paid personally to submit their own claim. Add a short note showing who ate what.
sam: The receipt just shows total €176 and "table 5". No line items. How do I allocate the business portion vs the personal dessert?
finance-maya: Good question. Preferred: ask restaurant for an itemized folio post-checkout. If not possible, add expense lines: 1) business meal €150, 2) personal dessert -€6 (negative) and attach a manager approval note. Include attendee names and an explanation like "Shared bottles + mains; personal dessert by Alex".
sam: Ok I can get manager approval. What about VAT? If there's no VAT line can Finance reclaim EU VAT?
finance-maya: If VAT is not shown on the receipt, we generally treat VAT as non-recoverable and reimburse the net. For small restaurant receipts sometimes VAT is embedded; we can't reclaim without a supplier tax ID and VAT breakdown. If you can get a stamped invoice from the restaurant later, upload it and we'll try reclaim.
manager-lee: I approve the split for Sam. Confirms business portion €150, personal €26 to Alex. Posting approval here so Finance has it.
sam: Thanks Lee. One more: I paid the bill in EUR but my card billed in GBP and bank conversion added rounding. Which amount do I claim?
finance-maya: Claim the original charged amount in the currency you paid (EUR) and attach the card statement line showing the conversion. Expensify will convert using the expense date rate; if there's a difference we'll reimburse the exact currency amount you were charged. Add a note: "charged €176 / billed £178.45 (bank conversion)".
sam: We also left a cash tip €15 to the server. Should I add that as a separate line?
people-ops: Yes, record tips as separate line items labeled "tip" and include reason. Keep tips reasonable per local custom. Cash tips are reimbursable.
sam: Cool. Finally, for client entertainment, do I need pre-approval or any additional forms?
people-ops: For meals under €300 per event no special pre-approval required beyond manager signoff on split items. For entertainment >€300 or any alcohol-heavy events, add a short business purpose note and get manager approval before submitting. Also tag the claim with "client-entertainment" project code.
expensify-bot: Auto-checklist: attach photo of handwritten receipt, include attendee list, attach card statement for conversion evidence, add manager approval for split items. Claims submitted by 17:00 PT processed in ~3 business days.
sam: Great, I'll upload the receipt, add the split lines and attach Lee's approval. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
